text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Majali holds talks in Cairo with Egypt's President Mubarak; they reaffirm need to achieve just and comprehensive peace in Middle East, and condemn Israel's settlement policies. Protocols and agreements signed and need for Arab economic solidarity stressed.
- Jordanian opposition parties send delegation from "Solidarity with Jerusalem" committee to Damascus for talks with Syrian officials.

- Jordan-Kuwait Bank extraordinary general assembly delayed until July 15 because it failed to achieve quorum of shareholders at meeting on Sunday after power struggle between rival shareholder groups.
- Jordan's Moslem Brotherhood head says there is internal dialogue, not dispute, within movement over whether to take part in parliamentary elections.
- Aqaba port authorities seek technical and financial presentations from six international consulting firms on plans to turn port into free trade zone.
- Majali says Jordan will boycott Middle East economic conference if other Arab states do.

- Cabinet agrees to float prices of frozen meat and fish, vegetable oil and food and drinks in cheap restaurants. Supply Ministry official says this will not lead to price rises because those commodities are plentiful.
- European parliamentary deputy bashes Spain's blocking of Jordan-EU partnership accord.
